prospect.name: Rudolph
prospect.aka: rtthompson21mac.com (speaker label is his email address)
prospect.location: Maryland, USA; originally from New York
prospect.occupation: Retired-and-rehired school counsellor working with middle school students aged 11-13; also a working football and basketball official and a track coach, with USATF-level coaching certifications. Currently studying for an additional qualification as a career hedge, and up for a five-year certificate renewal in May. Collects pensions alongside full-time salary; states his income is 'well over six figures'.
prospect.family_status: Widower, living alone for roughly the last four to seven years. Has lost five female family members in six or seven years — wife, sisters, cousins and mother-in-law. Says he hopes to be married again by 78.
prospect.training_background: Former high school and collegiate track athlete — his last 'tip-top shape' was 1974-75. Coached track and field at high school level in New York and collegiately for six years. Currently uses a rowing machine for 20-30 minutes regularly, rides a bike, has done free weights and machines, holds a Planet Fitness membership and has an apartment complex gym. Owns one kettlebell and a mobility stick, wants more kettlebells, and has watched Trevor's videos for about a year.
prospect.medical: Diabetic for 25 years, well managed — his doctors are 'flabbergasted' he has not developed the usual complications. Suspects possible kidney involvement related to the diabetes. Chronic lower back pain rated 4-5 out of 10, worst on waking, originating from repeatedly lifting his late wife into and out of a wheelchair after her herniated neck surgery; sees a chiropractor for it. Tendinitis on the top of his left foot and in his knee, under a podiatrist. Recent stress test passed with heart function 'well over 85%'. Cites a compromised family health history. Waist 40-42 inches, target 35-36.

signals: Proposed label: the_preserver — an older, health-literate, medically managed prospect with high nominal income but no liquidity, buying to hold ground and beat actuarial odds rather than to transform. None of the five listed avatars fit: he is not seeking a former self (explicitly rejects it — 'I don't want to be back to where I was in high school'), he is not price-insensitive, and no clinician has blocked him.

Goal is decline prevention framed statistically: 'I just don't want to be a statistic... the average age is 64, I already exceeded that. The next stage that I may encounter issues is 78. So I want to get to 78 standing and walking.'
Preservation over improvement — 'I don't want to lose what I have' and 'I don't expect to be performing like I was 20 and 30 years old'
Unusually health-literate and already medically supported: chiropractor, podiatrist, annual stress tests, rowing machine, sauna blanket, coaching certifications
The wealth-versus-liquidity split is the defining trait: over six figures of income and zero dollars available today

goals.text: Stay strong enough to keep working at his current pace for the next five to six years — 'my ultimate goal is probably the next five to six years is to continue working and to have the strength to continue at the pace that I'm working at'
Reach 78 still walking, driving and feeding himself without needing anyone's help — 'I don't want to get to a point where people have to do things for me'
Get his health markers consistent rather than fluctuating between check-ups
Lose the waist — from 40-42 inches down to 35-36, roughly 20-25 lb to around 200-205
Fix morning stiffness and improve overall flexibility and mobility
Keep running well enough to stay on the field as a football and basketball official and keep up with 11-13 year olds
Consistency in training — the thing he says he has never sustained since the gym requires him to leave his space
Learn kettlebell method well enough to add it to his coaching repertoire and teach it to young athletes
Be in shape to remarry — asked how achieving the goal would feel, his first answer was 'I would be married, hopefully'

pains.text: Diabetic for 25 years with suspected kidney involvement; doctors attribute his lack of complications to his activity levels
Chronic lower back pain from years of lifting his disabled late wife, rated 4-5 out of 10, worst on waking
Tendinitis in the top of the left foot and the knee, under podiatric care
Strength declines over the course of each year — 'as the year goes along, my strength goes down'

Watching peers his age decline — friends in their 80s 'sitting down because their legs are done', and a same-age friend just hospitalised in intensive care with a stroke

Living alone with all costs on one income; every dollar committed each month to rent, insurance and education loans
Officiating season from late August through November takes Wednesday to Saturday and will interfere with any schedule

objections.raw_quote: My current issue is I have access to that kind of money, but I don't have access to that at the moment... I'll be willing to do the 1,200 a month, but I have to wait until September... because I'm turning 70, my increase comes in September. So I need to probably wait to see what that increase is going to be. And that will free up the money.
objections.rep_response: Pushed back once — 'we don't want to wait per se until September' — then ran a proper cash probe (what is available now, whether there is anything left after bills, the $400 credit card) and, on establishing there was genuinely nothing, bridged with a $200/month self-study tier creditable against the full programme later.

objections.raw_quote: I don't have anything available right now... because a lot of my money is going out to pay because I'm living by myself. So all my payments went right out the door... I'm paying insurance, I'm paying rental, paying loans and stuff like that, because all the educational stuff.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and repeatedly reassured he would not push him into difficulty — 'I wouldn't want to put you in a financial position' — but then asked three separate times whether he could start immediately anyway, including probing the $400 emergency credit card.

objections.raw_quote: Okay, I was going to say, is it possible 1,000 a month? Is that a possibility?
objections.rep_response: Declined and held the line clearly: '$1,000 a month? No, it would be $1,200 a month' if split into six, with three payments of $2,000 as the alternative, stating plainly 'the price would increase with that'. The clearest and most honest instalment explanation in the batch.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Stated clearly and consistently for once: $6,000 flat, or three payments of $2,000 totalling $6,000, or six payments of $1,200 totalling $7,200 — with the rep saying explicitly 'the price would increase with that'. The prospect asked for $1,000/month and was refused. Separately, a $200/month self-study tier ($1,000 for six months) was offered as an entry point, with amounts paid credited toward the $1,200/month one-to-one programme when he upgrades in September.

prospect_financials.credit_score: not discussed; holds at least one credit card with $400 available which he reserves for emergencies, and mentions others carrying outstanding balances he is trying to clear

evidence: Verbal agreement in principle to start the $200/month self-study tier on Friday 31 July — 'by Friday, I will have that money available... I can break off $200 to get me started' and 'I'm glad to get started'
But no payment taken, no agreement sent and no payment link sent, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link close rule is not met
Rep asked three times to start immediately and was declined each time: 'No, let me just wait', 'Let me just be safe', 'No, I don't have that available'
Also agreed in principle to convert to the $1,200/month full programme in September once his Social Security increase lands, which he estimates at $4,000-6,000
No firm follow-up meeting booked — 'let's stay in contact', 'if it is on Friday, we can jump on on Friday, maybe', complicated by the rep travelling to Germany that day
Counter-evidence: genuinely strong intent throughout, and the prospect volunteered 'I want to do this'
Counter-evidence: he has zero liquidity today by his own account and reserves his only available credit for emergencies, so the Friday start depends entirely on a pay date he could not confirm
outcome.next_step: Rep to contact him Thursday 30 or Friday 31 July to take the first $200 self-study payment, after which an agreement and self-study access link would be sent; upgrade to the $1,200/month one-to-one programme to be revisited in September once his Social Security increase is confirmed.

notable.note: Escalate the medical issue. This prospect stated twice, unprompted, that he has been diabetic for 25 years — 'I also may be having some issues with my kidneys because I'm diabetic' at 00:10:57 and 'I've been diabetic for 25 years' at 00:22:12 — and the rep did not acknowledge it once, either time. A calorie-deficit nutrition protocol with restricted eating windows was then sold to him, which interacts directly with glycaemic control and medication timing, with no clinician mentioned and no screening question asked. He is also 69, turning 70 in twelve days, with suspected kidney involvement and chronic lumbar injury. This is the third unaddressed medical disclosure in this batch and the most consequential. Two other notes. The pricing was, unusually, quoted cleanly and honestly here: $6,000 flat, three payments of $2,000, or six of $1,200 with the rep stating outright that instalments cost more — which confirms the structure garbled on the Edward Garcia and Geoffrey calls. And the rep asked a man who had just said he has literally zero available and needs his last $400 for emergencies to start anyway, three separate times, including 'can I challenge you just to get started?'
